facts.fact: Adwave's own pricing page states that a TV campaign, including YouTube, starts at $30 a day.
facts.quote: A TV campaign, including YouTube, starts at $30 a day.

facts.fact: Adwave's own pricing page states that Google Search starts at $30 a day.
facts.quote: Google Search also starts at $30 a day.

facts.fact: Adwave's own pricing page states that daily budgets run from $30 to $10,000.
facts.quote: Daily budgets on that page run from $30 to $10,000.

facts.fact: The article says Adwave campaigns have no subscription and no contract.
facts.quote: There is no subscription and no contract.

facts.fact: In the article's example, a gym with $50 monthly memberships and 24-month average tenure has a $1,200 lifetime value per member.
facts.quote: A gym with $50 monthly memberships and 24-month average tenure has a $1,200 lifetime value per member.

facts.fact: The article says spending $100-200 to acquire a gym member makes sense given that member's $1,200 lifetime value in its example.
facts.quote: Spending $100-200 to acquire that member makes sense.

facts.fact: In the article's example, a customer spending $500 per year for five years has a $2,500 lifetime value.
facts.quote: spends $500 per year for five years ($2,500 lifetime value)

facts.fact: The article's example scenario assumes a customer acquisition cost of $75 each, which gives a $15,000 acquisition budget for 200 customers; the article labels this as an example, not a benchmark.
facts.quote: Example, not a benchmark: if you need 200 customers and you assume $75 each, the acquisition budget is $15,000.

facts.fact: The article says a reasonable total for its 200-customer example scenario might be $20,000-25,000.
facts.quote: A reasonable total might be $20,000-25,000 for this scenario.

facts.fact: The article's example revenue goal is to increase revenue from $300,000 to $400,000.
facts.quote: Increase revenue from $300,000 to $400,000

facts.fact: In the article's example, a customer spending $500 per year with a $100,000 new-revenue target implies 200 new customers.
facts.quote: If your average customer spends $500 per year and you want $100,000 in new revenue, you need 200 new customers.

facts.fact: The article suggests new businesses expect to spend at the higher end of ranges for their first two to three years.
facts.quote: Expect to spend at the higher end of ranges for your first two to three years.

facts.fact: The article recommends keeping 5-10% of the annual marketing budget unallocated for unexpected opportunities or competitive responses.
facts.quote: Keep 5-10% of your annual budget unallocated for unexpected opportunities or competitive responses.

facts.fact: The article gives an example split of 70% of the budget on proven channels, 20% on promising experiments, and 10% on brand building, labeled as one way to split it.
facts.quote: **70% on proven channels:** Spend the majority on what you know works.

facts.fact: In the article's example channel mix for local service businesses, 40% goes to Google Ads and local search.
facts.quote: 40% Google Ads and local search

facts.fact: In the article's example channel mix for local service businesses, 25% goes to reputation management and reviews.
facts.quote: 25% reputation management and reviews

facts.fact: In the article's example channel mix for local retail and restaurants, 30% goes to social media advertising.
facts.quote: 30% social media advertising

facts.fact: In the article's example channel mix for e-commerce, 35% goes to social media advertising.
facts.quote: 35% social media advertising

facts.fact: The article illustrates that a software company with 80% margins has more room for marketing than a restaurant with 10% margins on the same revenue.
facts.quote: A software company with 80% margins has more room for marketing than a restaurant with 10% margins on the same revenue.

facts.fact: Adwave says a campaign starts at $30 a day.
facts.quote: An Adwave campaign starts at $30 a day, so the restaurant TV line of $600 a month (about $20 a day) is below that published floor

facts.fact: Adwave says daily budgets on its pricing page run from $30 to $10,000.
facts.quote: Daily budgets on the pricing page run from $30 to $10,000.

facts.fact: The page's sample budget for a new local restaurant with $150,000 projected first-year revenue totals $30,000, which is 20% of projected revenue (an illustrative allocation, not an Adwave price).
facts.quote: $30,000 (20% of projected revenue)

facts.fact: The page's sample budget for an established dental practice with $1,000,000 revenue totals $80,000, which is 8% of revenue (an illustrative allocation, not an Adwave price).
facts.quote: $80,000 (8% of revenue)

facts.fact: The page's sample budget for a growth-focused home services company with $500,000 revenue (targeting $750,000) totals $75,000, which is 15% of revenue (an illustrative allocation, not an Adwave price).
facts.quote: $75,000 (15% of revenue)

facts.fact: In the page's sample dental practice budget, Google Ads is allocated $24,000 per year ($2,000 per month).
The page recommends that most small businesses allocate 70-80% of marketing budget to direct response.
facts.quote: lean toward direct response (70-80%) with a smaller allocation to brand building (20-30%)

facts.fact: The page states SEO typically shows results in 3-6 months.
facts.quote: SEO typically shows results in 3-6 months

facts.fact: The page states TV advertising often shows effects within 2-4 weeks.
facts.quote: TV advertising often shows effects within 2-4 weeks

facts.fact: The page advises reallocating a channel if nothing works after 90 days of systematic testing.
facts.quote: If nothing works after 90 days of systematic testing, reallocate.
